Source: Part G of the selected parent's supplied proof (G1: absolute convergence through A2a; G2–G6: bi-Lipschitz pieces, images, common approximate tangent planes, the signed integer multiplicity m and the IMRep), i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 3.5–3.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 857–865 for 3.9–3.10). The argument is organized piece by piece: for one Lipschitz map with an integrable integer weight, G2–G6 are the comparator-accepted sibling lipschitz_piece_im (its kernel-checked proof is the regular part, the approximately-linear bi-Lipschitz partition and the image currents of G2–G3, summed); the countable summation with common tangent planes, orientation signs and the integer multiplicity m (G4–G6) is the comparator-accepted sibling im_series; the weight bound G1 is the sibling gram_bounds (A2a). Hypothesis "finite total weight" replaces the supplied local bound (LF); it is exactly what the selected parent delivers through the sibling cone_parametrization.

Notation: 𝒟^{k+1} := TestFormOn univ (k + 1); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P), M(X) := X.mass = X.massOn univ, the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} with |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x.

1. (MR). The first conjunct of the sibling imrep_mass_support (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support) is: for U open, an IMRep R representing T' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every open W, T'.massOn W = R.measure W. This is the antecedent (MR) of the next two siblings.
2. (IMSc). Apply the sibling im_series (Submission.cmcdt_im_series) to its three antecedents: (VO) := the sibling support_vanishing (Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support), (MR) of step 1, and (IMC) := the sibling imrep_calculus (Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub). It yields (IMSc): for all P', k' and W : ℕ → 𝒟_{k'+1}(ℝ^{P'}) with Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞ there is Y ∈ 𝒟_{k'+1}(ℝ^{P'}) with HasSum (i ↦ W_i(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω, M(Y) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i), spt Y ⊆ closure ⋃_i spt W_i, and Y integer multiplicity whenever every W_i is.
3. Pieces (G2–G6 for one map). Apply the sibling lipschitz_piece_im (Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lpip_lipschitz_piece_current) to (MR), (IMC) and (IMSc). For each j, with H := F_j (Lipschitz with some constant L_j), A := A_j (Borel), g := g_j (measurable, integrable on A_j), it gives an integer multiplicity W_j ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with W_j(ω) = ∫_{A_j} g_j(u)·ω(F_j u)(∂F_j u) du for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}.
4. Mass of a piece (G1). M(W_j) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_j} |g_j|·JF_j. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} with |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x. For every u, the sibling gram_bounds (Submission.covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds), part (1), with α := ω(F_j u) and v := ∂F_j(u), gives |ω(F_j u)(∂F_j u)| ≤ |ω(F_j u)|_E·JF_j(u) ≤ JF_j(u). Hence ofReal(W_j(ω)) ≤ ‖W_j(ω)‖ₑ = ‖∫_{A_j} g_j ω(F_j)(∂F_j)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{A_j} ‖g_j(u)·ω(F_j u)(∂F_j u)‖ₑ du (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, valid without integrability) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_j} |g_j(u)|·JF_j(u) du. Taking the supremum over such ω gives the claim.
5. Summable masses. Σ_j M(W_j) ≤ Σ_j ∫⁻_{A_j} |g_j|·JF_j < ∞ by step 4 and the hypothesis.
6. Sum. By (IMSc) (step 2) with P' := P, k' := k and W := (W_j): there is Y ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (j ↦ W_j(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω, and Y is integer multiplicity because every W_j is (step 3).
7. Identification. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}, the sequence j ↦ W_j(ω) = ∫_{A_j} g_j ω(F_j)(∂F_j) has sum T(ω) (hypothesis) and sum Y(ω) (step 6); sums in ℝ are unique (HasSum.unique), so T(ω) = Y(ω). A GeometricCurrentOn is determined by its underlying linear functional (the continuity field is a proposition), hence T = Y, and T is integer multiplicity. ∎
